clue.text: Heathen confessing to swindling an ex-king

parts.note: someone confessing speaks in the first person, owning up with 'I'
to do someone is to swindle or cheat them
ex- is LATE (the late, former) and R is the abbreviation for rex, king

explanation.surface: A pagan owns up to having cheated a deposed monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The heathen's confession reads 'I do (swindle) the late R (king)'. Ex- as LATE, meaning former, is a standard crossword equivalence.
explanation.definitionFit: A worshipper of graven images is a pagan in the eyes of the monotheist, hence a heathen.

clue.text: I am a long time with 1 Ac's worshipful figures

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
ages means a long time

explanation.surface: Someone says they have been at the heathen's idols for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 Ac' points to the answer of 1 Across, the heathen, whose worshipped figures are idols.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolaters worship idols, carved or painted likenesses of gods.

clue.text: Heavenly paths of sovereigns, for instance ?

definitions.text: Heavenly paths of sovereigns, for instance

parts.words: Heavenly paths of sovereigns, for instance
parts.note: the circuits of the heavenly bodies, with a nod to the round orb a sovereign holds and the round gold sovereign coin

explanation.surface: Kings and queens are pictured taking a celestial route.
explanation.walkthrough: The circuits of planets around the sun are the paths in question; 'sovereigns' brings in the orb of royal regalia.
explanation.definitionFit: Planets and moons trace curved courses around larger bodies through space.

clue.text: Rugby players — ball perhaps is without

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the word before is only one possible arrangement of its letters

parts.note: lacks means is without

explanation.surface: Rugby players are left with no ball, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges BALL to ALLB, then LACKS (is without) follows. The All Blacks are New Zealand's national rugby union team.
explanation.definitionFit: The national rugby union side of New Zealand, named for its black kit.

clue.text: Sterile and as stormy as its Pacific setting belies

definitions.text: Sterile and as stormy as its Pacific setting belies

indicators.note: stormy means turbulent, so the letters of the preceding words are tossed about

explanation.surface: A barren, wind-lashed spot whose location on the peaceful ocean is misleading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stormy' rearranges STERILE AND AS. The whole clue is the description: a bleak, storm-battered island in the 'Pacific', a name meaning peaceful.
explanation.definitionFit: The remote, treeless island of the moai statues lies in the South Pacific, far off Chile.

clue.text: Furious with team membership going to a tear-away.

parts.note: mad means furious or angry
a cap is awarded for each appearance in a national team, so it stands for membership

explanation.surface: Someone angry at being picked for a side heads off to a wild youth.
explanation.walkthrough: In British sport a player 'gets a cap' for selection to the national side, so CAP signals team membership.
explanation.definitionFit: A madcap is a reckless, impulsive person, the same idea as a wild tear-away.

clue.text: Ghost's farewell in Hamlet

parts.note: the ghost of Hamlet's father leaves with the words 'remember me', preceded by a French goodbye said three times

explanation.definitionFit: The French goodbye is the parting word of old Hamlet's spirit in Act 1.

clue.text: London and Paris, for example, to start with

explanation.definitionFit: London and Paris are each a nation's seat of government; big letters at the start of a sentence or name are also so called.

clue.text: Represents red lights at sea?

parts.note: at sea the port side light is red
rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: A depiction of the navigation lamps of ships at night.
explanation.walkthrough: A ship shows a red light on its port (left) side; 'at sea' sets the nautical context.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray is to depict or represent in art or words.

clue.text: Weapon which may give a real stab

indicators.note: the letters of the next words may give, once rearranged, the weapon's name

explanation.surface: A dangerous weapon that could deliver a genuine stab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may give' signals that REAL STAB is rearranged; the 'a' before it is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbalest is a medieval crossbow, a missile-launching weapon.

clue.text: Baptist bird. ?

explanation.definitionFit: A Baptist immerses converts, so is jokily one who dunks; the dipper is a small bird that bobs and dives in streams.

clue.text: Inexorably, but still serenely, without a single disturbance

indicators.note: a disturbance stirs up the letters of the words before

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral, means a single one

explanation.surface: Unstoppably, yet calmly, without ruffling anything at all.
explanation.walkthrough: STILL SERENELY minus one I ('without a single'), stirred by 'disturbance', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexorably means without yielding or easing up, unstoppably.

clue.text: Praise is out of context, old boy

indicators.note: the letters wanted are taken out of the run of words that follows, spanning their joins

explanation.surface: Commendation quoted out of context, old chap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is out of' signals a hidden word: it runs from the end of 'context' into 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to laud or exalt, a verb for giving high commendation.

clue.text: Government's recognition of former hot line, say

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: say signals that the following phrase is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: the equator is the hot line circling the earth's middle

explanation.surface: A state acknowledges what used to be an emergency telephone link.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you EQUATOR is only matched in sound by the spelling EQUATUR. The surface 'hot line' looks like a direct telephone link between leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: An exequatur is the official document by which a state recognises a foreign consul and permits them to act.

clue.text: Sharps and flats so played by unskilled pianists?

definitions.text: Sharps and flats so played by unskilled pianists?

parts.words: Sharps and flats so played by unskilled pianists?
parts.note: sharps and flats in a score are accidentals; a poor player hits them by chance rather than design

explanation.surface: Clumsy amateurs bungle the black notes on the keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes not in the key signature are termed accidentals, and an unskilled pianist plays them by mistake, by chance.

clue.text: But not an alternative to the matutinal brush

definitions.text: But not an alternative to the matutinal brush

parts.words: But not an alternative to the matutinal brush
parts.note: the morning brush suggests a toothbrush; this grooming tool shares its first word yet is no substitute for one

explanation.surface: A remark that some item cannot replace the morning brushing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matutinal' means of the morning; the morning brush is the toothbrush, and a fine comb, despite its name, is no alternative to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine comb with close-set teeth, used for searching closely, shares the first word of the morning brush.

clue.text: A party, piece concerning this summons

indicators.note: this points at the answer: the party piece is made of 'concerning' plus this, so removing the first part leaves it

parts.note: a recitation is a party piece, a poem recited to guests
re means concerning, about

explanation.surface: Someone is called to perform their party piece, a reading about the summons.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'A party piece (RECITATION) is concerning (RE) + this (the answer)'; take RE off RECITATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A citation is an official summons to appear in court.

clue.text: " With such prophetic -" the witches stopped Macbeth

definitions.text: " With such prophetic -" the witches stopped Macbeth

parts.words: " With such prophetic -" the witches stopped Macbeth
parts.note: Macbeth asks the witches why they stop his way 'with such prophetic' words of salutation

explanation.surface: A quotation from Macbeth with its last word blanked.
explanation.walkthrough: In Act 1 Macbeth demands why the witches 'stop our way With such prophetic' hailing; fill the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: The witches hail Macbeth with titles, a salutation that foretells his future.

clue.text: Macbeth was exhorted to be bloody bold without it

definitions.text: Macbeth was exhorted to be bloody bold without it

parts.words: Macbeth was exhorted to be bloody bold without it
parts.note: the apparition tells Macbeth 'Be bloody, bold and resolute', so he must lack any wavering

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's Scottish king was urged to be bloodthirsty and fearless with no hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: In Macbeth Act 4 the second apparition says 'Be bloody, bold, and resolute'; being resolute means being without its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecision or wavering is the opposite of being resolute, which Macbeth was told to be.

clue.text: Odds on the right tool being used to spread out

parts.note: SP, starting price, is the odds offered on a racehorse
R is the abbreviation for right
an awl is a pointed tool for piercing holes

explanation.surface: A punter's odds on the right implement for spreading things out.
explanation.walkthrough: SP (starting price) is a British betting term for the odds at the start of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprawl is to spread out untidily, as limbs or a town do.

clue.text: Not flowing like water

explanation.walkthrough: British towns in the Second World War had tanks marked EWS, Emergency Water Supply, often called static water tanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Static means motionless; in wartime Britain a fire-fighting reservoir was labelled static water.

clue.text: Bearer can be put out by deviation

indicators.note: put out means disordered, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A porter might be upset by someone straying off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be put out' rearranges BEARER and CAN together; 'by' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberrance is a straying from the normal path, a departure from the norm.

clue.text: A bird — about the first one

parts.note: re means about, concerning
Eve was the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: A bird circling the very first one there was.
explanation.walkthrough: The reeve is the female ruff, a wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The female of the ruff, a sandpiper, is called by this name.

clue.text: How to play the Scotch game ? Get away !

definitions.text: How to play the Scotch game

explanation.walkthrough: The 'Scotch game' is hopscotch, the playground game: 'hop it' is how you play it.
explanation.definitionFit: In hopscotch you must hop on the squares, so the instruction for the game is to hop; as slang, hop it is a brusque order to clear off.

clue.text: Flowers — but only one comes up

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
rises means comes up, as the sun does

explanation.surface: A bed of blooms, but only a single bulb has sprouted.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a gardener's disappointment; read the wordplay as one (I) rises.
explanation.definitionFit: Irises are garden plants with showy blooms, such as the flag.

clue.text: Using the same vowel sounds as a boy worker

parts.note: a son is a boy
the ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A lad employed somewhere speaks with uniform vowels.
explanation.walkthrough: The ant is the conventional worker in crosswords (from the worker ant).
explanation.definitionFit: Assonance is the rhyme of vowel sounds alone, so an assonant line repeats its vowel sounds.

clue.text: Horse in poor tune gets the gold

indicators.note: in places the horse inside the rearranged letters
poor means badly done, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: gee-gee, GG, is a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: A racehorse wins gold despite a badly played tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges TUNE to NUET, and 'in' puts GG inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A nugget is a lump of native gold, so stands for the gold itself.

clue.text: Slim boy worried about description of signs

indicators.note: worried means disturbed, so the letters of the next words are rearranged

parts.note: c, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A thin lad is anxious about how to describe certain signals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges SLIMBOY to SYMBOLI; C (circa) follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Symbolic means standing for or representing something, as signs and emblems do.
